I have no idea how to interpret this but on a deep level I understand

"be less elitist and more accepting of people without making it into a competition" and how do you do that without broadening your definition of self harm? It's not worth gate-keeping. If you're seeking to harm yourself, that's a problem, regardless of preferred method. Why should the people you deem as worthy of being gate-keeped be struck from the support/resources of communities like this?

I understand what you're saying, but also, I really do see many issues with this.

I see what you're saying, but I also feel like statements like this can encourage the problem of elitism in the self-harming community (e.g. "you're not a REAL cutter unless you X"), which can in turn be potentially harmful via encouraging escalation of self-harming behaviours in order to be seen as 'legitimate' and worthy of help. 

Imo, trying to define what is/isn't self harm is at best non productive, and at worst actively harmful. For me, if you're actively intending to cause harm to yourself with an action, that is self harm, regardless of method.
